page.layout: One page of text. Running head at top left, page number at top right. Verse block in roman with italic lines, followed by an indented prose paragraph and a second prose paragraph. Signature at the foot right. No marginal notes.

p.i: Quippe ubi fas uerfum, atq; nefas, tot bella per orbe Tam multæ fcelerum facies, non ullus aratro Pignus honos, fqualent, abductis arua colonis, Et curuæ rigidum falces conflantur in enfem.
-Cedit uiribus æquum, Vict[?]aq; pugnaci iura fub enfe iacent.

main_text.p: A violenta irruptione, & thrafonica in urbem Ierusalem cum hoftibus Chaldæis triumphantibus de Iudæa capta, ingresfio-ne, Obadias noster feriò dehortatur Idu-mæos, quum ait: Ne ingrediaris portam populi mei die calamitatis eorum, ne afpicias tu quoq; malum eius die calamitatis ipsius. Qui enim gente aliqua bello deuicta, triumphantium hostium, cateruis fese adiungunt, & fpectatores agunt tum hostilis insolentiæ, tum calamitatum in quas vi inciderunt: & oculos pascunt, non cogitantes de rerum humanarum instabilitate & vicissitudinibus: nec commiserantes oppressorum miserias, illis certè & pectora sunt Caucasi rupibus asperiora & duriora: & imminent grauissimæ pœnæ.
A rapinis autem itidem dehortatur Idu-mæos, quum addit in posteriore hemistichio: Neq; extendant fe(manus) in facultates eius die calamitatis eius.

page.notes: The verse "Victaq;" is set in a ligature that is hard to read; the reading is uncertain. "deuicta" is read from the split form "deui-/cta" and is uncertain. The word "vi" before "inciderunt" is partly obscured. The mark "Q.V.I-" at the foot is read as the gathering signature. No other marginal text is printed.
